key_insight: Transient ion current (TIC/BACE) in perovskite solar cells is often limited not by the absorber’s ions, but by the charge-capacitance of the transport layers that must store the compensating charge.
engineering_relevance: Accurate ion-density extraction requires accounting for transport-layer thickness and capacitance, otherwise TIC can overestimate ionic properties by orders of magnitude across PSC architectures.
method: Varied C60 electron-transport-layer thickness in p-i-n devices
Varied Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport-layer doping in n-i-p devices
Used simulations and trend extrapolation to infer absorber ionic parameters and assess transport-layer-free limits
evidence_signal: Experiments across systematically changed transport-layer conditions showed TIC depends strongly on transport-layer properties, and the abstract reports that extrapolating these trends can recover ionic conductivity, density, and mobility depending on the model.
watch_item: TIC-based ion quantification can be inflated by transport-layer capacitance, ion penetration into transport layers, or slow trapped-carrier release, so raw TIC signals should not be interpreted directly as absorber ion density.
paper_title: Overcoming Transport Layer Bottlenecks to Quantify Ionic Parameters from Transient Ion Current Measurements of Perovskite Solar Cells
